shared_elements: a horizontal band filled with repeated short vertical strokes
justification: The most specific correspondence is that both surfaces organise their imagery into stacked horizontal registers and both contain a long band subdivided by repeated short vertical strokes (the incised zigzag/comb band on A, the crew strokes above the hull on B), plus small profile animals and human-like figures. The overriding difference is the technique and format: A is a deeply carved, three-dimensional relief on a tall upright block with volumetric, individually modelled beasts, whereas B is a flat, monochrome red linear drawing spread over a broad sloping rock face dominated by boat forms with no relief at all.
